_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. governance.md is preserved by onboard.py --resume but a FULL reprint re-runs gen_governance.py and would re-introduce the mis-tiering.

handfixes.summary: Hand-added a 'Physical / device control' tier; gen_governance files Domotz's hardware-action verbs (power-action/outlet/onvif/vpn) into Read because they carry no write keyword
handfixes.why: gen_governance.py keyword-matches command paths, so Domotz's device-action verbs that mutate real hardware (power outlets, cameras, VPN tunnels) - `power-action-on`, `trigger-outlet-action`, `attach-to-outlet`/`detach-from-outlet`, `onvif-snapshot`, `connect-to`, `backup-configuration`, `create-agent-vpnconnection` - carry no write keyword and fell into Read/Allow. A network-monitoring/RMM connector with hardware control needs a human-in-the-loop Physical tier. A full reprint re-runs gen_governance and drops these back to Read. See project_domotz_onboard_gotchas.

handfixes.summary: `agent device get-snmpauthentication` is a secret-returning READ; moved to the Credential tier, not Read/Allow
handfixes.why: Its response schema (SNMPDomotzAuthentication) includes snmp_read_community, snmp_write_community, authentication_key, encryption_key - a secret-returning read, the SNMP sibling of the itglue passwords-get case. It must NOT be Read/Allow. (The plain `agent device get` has no typed schema and does NOT return community strings, so it correctly stays Read.) A full reprint's keyword classifier would file get-snmpauthentication as a benign get. See feedback_secret_read_commands_not_read_tier.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For domotz the manifest gained: DOMOTZ_BASE_URL. server.json gained: DOMOTZ_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: DOMOTZ_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 1 command listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs it
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: agent network add-excluded-device (POST /agent/{agent_id}/network/excluded-device/{device_id}).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name, and no file stores operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds; applied by tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py. The <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Each operator-named write (profiles.json, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl and the learn tables: learnings, playbooks, candidates, recall misses, entity aliases, patterns) goes through the credential kit's file or SQL sink, which withholds one that carries a credential the program holds. journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>. The connector's own RefuseHeld checks on each journal, log, profile, feedback, learning, playbook, candidate, lookup and pattern write are replaced by the kit's sinks (credkit-wiring, credkit-sqlite-every-handle), so every line that does reach a file passes the kit's matcher as one unit.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: Every resource write passes withoutStoredSecrets (internal/store/stored_secret_fields.go), which masks every credential-named value by the one secret-name rule (cliutil.RedactSecretFields), so a device is kept with its SNMP communities masked, an SNMP v3 authentication with its user and keys masked and a custom driver association with its credentials masked. Every SQL statement then passes the kit's SQL driver (credkit-sqlite-every-handle).
handfixes.why: Work order: no credential in files. The kit's SQL driver withholds a whole statement that carries a held value, and the SNMP communities, keys and driver credentials are held response fields, so without the mask a sync of devices would store nothing. TestDeviceCredentialsNeverPrint checks the record is stored, masked. The old storedID rewrite and withhold driver are retired with the old layer.

handfixes.summary: A config rewrite adds no credential to config.toml: config.toml keeps its own base_url, never DOMOTZ_BASE_URL's (configForSave), so a userinfo password or query credential in DOMOTZ_BASE_URL never lands in the file; a saved token goes to the 0600 credential store. config.toml and the store are credential SOURCES (orchestrator ruling 7): written outside the kit through cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, named in Declarations.Files and held whole on every read and write.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 class credential-persisted-outside-the-store: `DOMOTZ_BASE_URL='https://api-us-east-1-cell-1.domotz.com/public-api/v1?api_key=X' auth set-token` wrote X (and a userinfo password) into config.toml, because the generated save persists base_url as configured. The old persistence filter (domotz_persist.go) is retired with the old layer; the source-side fix is that a rewrite keeps the file's own values. TestP1ConfigRewriteAddsNoCopyOfTheURLPassword covers the environment password beside a [headers] value; TestConfigFileNeverHoldsACredential (black box) the query credential.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file (written through the kit's credkit.NewWriter) on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. Under the retired output filter the unclosed file was a pipe that kept the process from exiting (`export custom-driver --output drivers.jsonl` after a 401 hung; TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError); the kit's writer is closed on the same path.

handfixes.summary: The X-API-KEY header and every API request go only to the scheme, host and port of the configured base URL (https://api-us-east-1-cell-1.domotz.com/public-api/v1, or DOMOTZ_BASE_URL); every redirect hop must stay on that origin, a non-ASCII host never matches, and an unparseable base URL pins nothing (every request refused). Installed on every CLI, novel and MCP client by registerClientHook (internal/cli/domotz_guard.go), with the response cache off and --dry-run clients refusing every send
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: the generated client sends the X-API-KEY header to whatever URL it is handed and its CheckRedirect strips only the named auth headers, so a Location to another host or an absolute path from an MCP argument would carry the key off the vendor API. One origin, taken from the configured base URL; an operator who sets DOMOTZ_BASE_URL moves the pin with it. Ported to domotz from the atera 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Ported to domotz from the betterstack 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: The identity half of a Domotz credential pair is a credential: username (a device's credentials, the SNMP v3 user, a custom driver association's credentials) is a declared CredentialField, ResponseField and MCPArgument, and the credential flags --username and --credentials-username are declared, so the kit holds it before any sink; the one secret-name rule (credentialIdentityName) reads the same names so the store and an MCP preview mask it. Names that only mention users (user_id, an activity log's user, last_login_at) stay visible.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] holder incomplete, ported from the betterstack review: the user beside a password matched no credential rule. TestDeviceCredentialsNeverPrint runs the SNMP v3 user and the driver login on the built binaries against a TLS fake.

handfixes.summary: Every config file any --config on the command line names is held inside credkit.Start, before any output (credentialFiles: holdOnly(runFiles(cfg)) for each), so a config the parser never reached cannot print in an unknown-command or flag error.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] alternate-config credentials unheld: the startup holder loaded only DOMOTZ_CONFIG or the default path, so `domotz-cli <token> --config alt.toml` printed alt.toml's api_key in its unknown-command error. MCP cannot reach the read (domotz-mcp has no --config and refuses one). The old startup holder is retired with the old layer; TestBsR1CommandLineConfigIsHeldBeforeParse (black box) and TestMalformedConfigNeverPrintsAtStartup run on the built binaries.

handfixes.summary: The origin pin is the resolved templated base URL (https://api-{region}.domotz.com/public-api/v1 with DOMOTZ_REGION filled in), and a region that is not one DNS label pins nothing, so every request is refused
handfixes.why: The ported guard pinned url.Parse(c.BaseURL); the unresolved {region} template does not parse, the pin was empty and every request was refused. pinnedOrigin resolves the template first and refuses a region that could change the host (a dot, a slash, an @). Test seen failing first: seen/region-origin-pinned-seen-failing.log in the run dir. (domotz 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: The credential-name rule and the kit's declarations are pinned against Domotz's own spec names in both directions (cliutil/testdata/domotz-spec-names.json): of every spec name exactly X-Api-Key, authentication_key, credentials, encryption_key, password, read, snmp_read_community, snmp_write_community, username and write read as credentials, and the declared ResponseFields and CredentialFields are those names but the X-Api-Key header (a CredentialHeader); MCPArguments add each credential flag's spelling. key, user, vpn_session_id and the authentication_status/type/protocol names stay visible (publicSecretLikeFields).
handfixes.why: Class over-withholding of product data and press-traps s2: a name-based rule read Domotz inventory keys, activity log users and authentication enums as credentials, and a spec-name guard that reads a spec file skips where none ships. Pinned names cannot skip. TestDomotzPublicFieldsAreNotWithheld (black box) prints the public fields from the CLI and MCP and finds them in the store.

handfixes.summary: The SNMP v1/v2 communities Domotz names bare read and write (DeviceSnmpCommunity, PUT /agent/{agent_id}/device/{device_id}/snmp-community) are declared credential fields, response fields, MCP arguments and credential flags (--read, --write), so the kit holds them whatever their type: a whitespace-only string and a number included. The one secret-name rule reads bare read and write as credential names; a number under them in data the program reads (rows read) stays a count to the mask (countLikeName), so a preview carrying such a number is withheld whole by the kit.

handfixes.why: Codex review round 1 (domotz 4.34.2) class wrong-field-read on documented shapes: fleet inventory, breakdown and new read vendor/model only from user_data (DeviceUserDataModel), so a device Domotz detected as Cisco C9300 (LocalIpDevice vendor, model) read as unknown; fleet agents read location.name, which AgentLocation never has, and printed the AgentVersion object. handfixes.summary: Every Domotz timestamp a novel compares or orders goes through one parser (parseDomotzTime) and is compared as an instant: fleet new filters and sorts first_seen_on in Go, fleet speedtest picks the latest NetworkSpeedSample, fleet events orders the activity log
handfixes.why: Codex review round 1 (domotz 4.34.2) class time-compared-as-text on documented shapes (ISO 8601 with a timezone offset): fleet speedtest compared NetworkSpeedSample timestamps as strings, so 12:00+02:00 (10:00Z) beat 11:00Z and the fleet report used a stale 1 Mbps sample; fleet new compared first_seen_on to the cutoff in SQL text order. Same class in the store's own stamps: topology cached its row with CURRENT_TIMESTAMP while sync stamps network_topology RFC3339, so topology --cached ordered the text and read the older sync row within a day (seen/r1-time-compared-as-text-topology-seen-failing.log); the cache now stamps RFC3339 and the read picks the newest row as an instant. fleet speedtest also returns a decode error for an unreadable answer instead of reading it as no data. handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit, and every early exit of the MCP main returns through it; the API client (client.OutboundGuard, under the origin pin), feedback, deliver and probe clients go through credkit.Transport; every file write outside the 0600 credential store and config goes through the kit (response and platform cache, export, deliver, feedback, journal, teach logs, run profiles, client profiles, the legacy-store claim marker, the rate-limit stamp); the MCP stdio and HTTP servers pass credkit.MCPIn, MCPOut, MCPHTTP and MCPTools; the MCP mirror runs the CLI with credkit.RunCommand; stdout is asked about through credkit.Terminal. The store and config rewrites go outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile) as declared credential sources. A config or credential file is held with credkit.HoldBody and credkit.HoldURL every time it is read, a token read from a pipe is held as stdin, a dry-run preview's body is held (cliutil.HoldBody) before it prints, a built auth header and a resolved client-profile value are held where they enter, and the MCP server's --tls-key file is held at startup. A run profile treats a flag the one secret-name rule names as a credential flag. The base URL is a template (https://api-{region}.domotz.com/public-api/v1): credwire resolves it with config.Load and hands the kit the one host this run uses through DOMOTZ_BASE_URL for Start alone (RestoreStartupEnv puts it back). domotz_execute's confirmation preview masks credential-named values (mcp-endpoint-write-confirm), and the black box under internal/domotzblackbox keeps the domotz behavior cases (origin pin, region, MCP confirm, dry run, public field names).
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. It closes the open P1 whitespace-credential-encoded-echo (a device whose display_name is the base64 of its whitespace-only SNMP read community: TestP1WhitespaceCommunityEncodedEchoNeverPrints, seen failing on the pre-kit build, .review/whitespace-p1-evidence.log) and the open review classes: doctor's credentials verdict (no name-based redaction), the env-schema gate (no EnvOverride holder over every variable), and the MCP HTTP no-token refusal printed before os.Exit (credkit.Exit drains it). Tests: internal/credwire/leak_test.go, on the built binaries (DOMOTZ_LEAK_BIN_DIR runs them against another build). Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, secure-container-is-credential, r1-holder-reads-every-part, r1-mixed-byte-escapes-decoded, r1-split-across-deliveries-withheld, held-value-case-folded, output-units-reassembled, preclose-holder-numbers-and-cookies, preclose-escape-fixpoint, preclose-split-across-processes-and-protocol, refuse-held-uses-connector-chokepoint, output-derived-and-scheme-forms-matched-whole, g304-paths-cleaned-not-annotated, r1-short-value-encodings-withheld, r1-file-history-is-the-whole-file, r2-short-value-nested-encodings, response-credentials-held, r1-credential-split-across-deliveries, r1-decoder-bound-read-as-no-echo, r1-persistence-gate-narrower-than-chokepoint, startup-error-lost, r1-short-held-value-inside-other-text, r1-secret-in-headerless-compressed-stream, r1-unreadable-history-read-as-empty, r1-check-then-append-not-serialized, r1-mask-shaped-credential, r2-whitespace-credential, credential-named-by-sibling-member: replaced by the shared credential kit (listed under _superseded). The kit holds every contract section 1 source at startup and on arrival, and withholds at every sink as one stream, so the connector's own holder, decoded funnel, output chokepoint, file and network writers, SQL withhold driver, store stripping, argv refusal and whitespace marker rule are gone, with their tests.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing, then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the inner, kit-wrapped handler and only a write-free preflight runs before credkit.MCPHTTP.

handfixes.summary: --stdin is a declared StdinFlag, so the kit holds a body whole and line by line before anything prints. cliutil.CompactStdinBody puts a JSON body on one line first, because a line of { alone collides with public text and refuses the start. feedback --stdin refuses instead of reporting a record the kit would withhold.
handfixes.why: A device credentials, SNMP or custom driver association body (agent device set-credentials, set-snmp-community, set-snmpauthentication, custom-driver agent create-custom-driver-association --stdin) carries the device's credentials, and a held body is the kit's to judge. The cost: a --dry-run preview of a --stdin body, and a vendor answer repeating part of it, are withheld whole, and the write still happens.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate StdinFlags and the compaction with the kit wiring.

handfixes.summary: credentialFiles returns the config the program really uses first, because the kit takes the base URL and every allowed origin from the first file naming one: an explicit --config or DOMOTZ_CONFIG wins, the last --home decides the default paths, and every other file any flag could mean is only held. The credential stores and run profile stores are only held too: config.Load takes no base URL from a store. Startup reads --config and --home by every occurrence; the root pre-run refuses a run whose parsed values differ (another flag swallowed one), so a file the run does not use never names the allowed origin. domotz-mcp, which has no such flags, refuses to start when startup read one. The base URL is a template: selectKitBaseURL resolves the config this run uses (config.Load with the kit's holds off) to its one regional host and hands it to Start through DOMOTZ_BASE_URL, restored right after Start (RestoreStartupEnv); a region that is not one DNS label leaves the unparsable template, so every credential is refused.
handfixes.why: A discovered default's or a store's base_url must not become an allowed origin for a credential from another file.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the file discovery in the wiring file.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.
